claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings provide zirconium-alloy cladding with oxidation protection.
Elemental Cr coatings provide good oxidation resistance under both normal PWR water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
Cr coatings can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
High-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 1–5 atomic % Al to an otherwise elemental Cr coating.
Al or Si should be considered in the design of accident-tolerant cladding materials for high-temperature steam oxidation.
CrAl coatings are among the metallic protective coatings investigated for zirconium-alloy cladding.
Adding 1–5 atomic % Al to Cr will cause a thin, stable Al2O3 layer to form at the Cr/Zr interface.
Al in the doped coating will preferentially oxidize at high temperature.
The resulting Al2O3 layer will be dense and stable under the proposed exposures.
An interfacial Al2O3 layer will suppress Cr and Zr atomic mobility across the coating/substrate interface.
Suppressing Cr and Zr mobility will reduce the width of the Cr–Zr interdiffusion zone during high-temperature steam exposure.
Al doping will retain the oxidation protection inherently provided by Cr under subcritical PWR-water conditions.
The Al-doped coating will provide corrosion or oxidation performance equivalent to the undoped Cr coating under normal PWR conditions.
The combined reduction in interdiffusion and retention of oxidation protection will improve overall coating durability.
The proposed benefit applies in PWR primary water at approximately 300–350 °C.
The proposed benefit applies in accident-relevant steam above 1000 °C and up to approximately 1200 °C.
The optimum Al concentration and long-term stability of the proposed Al2O3 barrier have not been established.
Performance and barrier stability under prolonged neutron irradiation remain uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits oxidation/corrosion performance equivalent to the undoped coating under normal PWR conditions, whereas the falsification rule declares unchanged performance under any exposure condition to be falsifying.
